- the diff: <scratchpad>/c2.diff (commit edff89b, a move of aven/DB2/sandbox/box/Dockerfile and .github/workflows-avendb/avensandbox-image.yml with edits)
- the files as they stand: /home/user/maiacity/theOS/sandbox/box/Dockerfile and /home/user/maiacity/.github/workflows/avensandbox-image.yml (also theOS/sandbox/run.sh, which computes the same tag).

Questions: Does the work keep c2's promise and make its check possible (built only from theOS/sandbox/box, amd64 and arm64, tagged by the hash of that folder and the workflow, same inputs never build twice, every tool working, smoke proves it)? Correctness bugs in the workflow (job conditions, outputs, permissions, the tag, the "already built" test, failure paths, concurrency, the latest tag)? Anything in the Dockerfile that reads outside its context, is unpinned, or is stale avenDB text that now misleads? Security for a public repository (secrets, injection, permissions)?

For each finding give: Severity (Blocker | Major | Nit), kind (one of: bug, wrong fact, unclear, contradiction, YAGNI, security, missing check), the affected file and line, the reasoning, and a concrete fix. Give evidence a reader can verify. At most 600 words, plain text, no praise, lead with what is wrong. If there is no Blocker or Major, say so plainly.

findings.text: latest needed only plan and publish, so main's box was tagged latest even when the smoke step failed; and a failed build skips publish, which the 'skipped' clause read as 'already built', so smoke and latest ran against a tag never published.
findings.note: latest needs smoke and runs only when smoke succeeded; smoke runs when the plan found both platforms built or publish succeeded; always() replaced by !cancelled().

findings.text: c2 promises every tool works on both platforms, but smoke ran only on an amd64 runner; the arm64 image the Mac runs was never smoked.
findings.note: smoke runs in the same matrix as build (ubuntu-24.04 and ubuntu-24.04-arm), with docker run --platform linux/<arch>, and prints uname -m.

findings.scope: c2's check: same inputs build nothing
findings.text: Never exercised: only the first build is recorded, and the later commits did not trigger the workflow.
findings.note: A workflow_dispatch on the same commit as a finished build; its run is recorded in AIP-2's events.

findings.scope: Dockerfile header: every version is pinned
findings.text: The playwright base was a mutable tag; apt packages and the rustup and elan installers are unpinned.
findings.note: The base is pinned by digest (sha256:47b510dd..., what v1.64.1-noble points at today, read with docker buildx imagetools inspect); the header now says what is pinned and what is not.

findings.text: Comments named avenDB's store, compose.yml, the Peer-Light, db/docs/README.md and sandbox/fuzz.sh, none of which exist in theOS.
findings.note: Each tool's comment now says what it does and that it is kept with every tool (D-33).

findings.text: The workflow and run.sh each computed the tag, and the image name differed in source; nothing checked that they agree.
findings.note: One script, theOS/sandbox/tag.sh, used by both; it printed the same tag as before (theos-4d9bc364ffc5f836) on the same commit.

findings.text: In jobs with packages: write, a moved tag could push a poisoned image under the public name.
findings.note: Every action pinned to its commit, read with git ls-remote, with the version in a comment.

findings.text: The smoke step depends on npm at test time; that should be said.
findings.note: A comment says why: the image holds the browser, not the package.

rounds.result: 2 Major, 5 Nit: not clean. The fixes of round 1 hold; both Majors are runs not yet on record.

findings.scope: c2 on both platforms at the current inputs
findings.text: Round 1's arm64 smoke and the new latest gating had not run on GitHub; the only build on record was for the old tag, smoked on amd64 only.
findings.note: Run 41295874265 (push of 649608d) built theos-7f2a978d8e9df74f; round 3's inputs are built and smoked on both platforms by a new run, recorded in the events with its id.

findings.text: Round 1's answer (a workflow_dispatch on the same commit) had not happened yet.
findings.note: Dispatched on the same commit after the push's run finished; its run id, the plan's 'has: amd64,arm64' and the skipped builds recorded in the events.

findings.text: The workflow and run.sh take the tag from tag.sh, but a change to it neither triggers the workflow nor changes the tag.
findings.note: tag.sh is in the push paths and in the hash.

findings.scope: a tag exists before its smoke
findings.text: publish tagged the box before smoke, so a box that failed smoke stayed pullable and was never rebuilt.
findings.note: The smoke step moved into each build job: it runs the platform's image by digest before the digest is kept, so a failing box is never joined and never tagged; the separate smoke job is gone, and latest waits for publish (or the box built and smoked before).

findings.text: The platform was printed, not asserted.
findings.note: The smoke step fails unless uname -m is x86_64 on amd64 and aarch64 on arm64.

findings.text: Two branches pushing the same new inputs at once both build them.
findings.note: Said in a comment above concurrency: the same image twice, harmless; one after another, the second builds nothing.

findings.text: An edited header line ran to about 180 characters.
findings.note: The header is re-wrapped to the file's width.
